NOT THIS PR'S BUG, recorded because it bears on PR #62. `python3 scripts/lwb_check_proof.py --reexecute` exits 1 at this head: 'proof/39.json: python3 scripts/lwb_handoff.py --check: digest mismatch'. I checked before charging it to this PR: the SAME failure is present on a clean worktree of origin/main at 0d1be71 (re-run digest 4752247... on main vs ded08fb... here, both against the same recorded ab8f5e3...), so it is pre-existing. The PR author independently found and disclosed this in 9b310f2's own commit message, which matches my measurement. Root cause, which I did check: lwb_handoff.py --check's output embeds HANDOFF.md's byte count ("passes all checks (2975 bytes)" here, "(2960 bytes)" on main), so its recorded digest cannot survive ANY edit to HANDOFF.md and that command can never be legitimately verifiable: true. This is currently harmless -- the lwb-proof-reexecute step is continue-on-error/report-only -- but PR #62 makes that step blocking, at which point this pre-existing mismatch becomes a hard failure. Flagging it for #62, not against #69.

NEAR-MISS, AND A CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST EXPLANATION OF IT -- BOTH RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. My first baseline run reported '1 failed, 608 passed' on origin/main (tests/test_lwb_lanes.py::test_is_record_only_commit_true_for_a_merge_with_empty_first_parent_diff) and I was one step from filing "main is red". I had launched the base and head pytest runs concurrently, so I assumed a measurement artifact of my own making, re-ran in isolation, got 609 passed, and WROTE THAT CONCLUSION INTO AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS RECORD. That conclusion was WRONG, and I am correcting it here rather than quietly shipping it, because it would have buried a real defect under an apology for my own tooling.

The test is genuinely FLAKY, and its flakiness is a TRUE POSITIVE. Measured: the full suite at this head fails it roughly 1 run in 3 (three consecutive full runs: 615 passed, 615 passed, 1 failed/614 passed), with no random-order plugin installed (pytest 9.1.1, plugin list empty -- collection order is deterministic). tests/test_lwb_lanes.py run ALONE passes 5/5 in ~5s; the full suite takes ~28s.

ROOT CAUSE, reproduced deterministically rather than inferred. The test builds a temp repo, commits a substantive mainline change, commits an unrelated change on a side branch, then `git merge --no-ff -s ours`, and asserts resolve_reviewable_head returns the MAINLINE substantive commit. resolve_reviewable_head (as it stands on main) walks `git log --format=%H <head>`, which walks ALL parents in commit-date order. When the test runs fast enough that the substantive and side commits land in the SAME second, git's tie-break follows parent order and the mainline commit is emitted first, so the test passes. When the machine is loaded (the full suite) and the side commit crosses into a later second, git emits the SIDE commit first and resolve_reviewable_head returns it. I built that case explicitly with forced GIT_AUTHOR_DATE/GIT_COMMITTER_DATE one second apart (/tmp flakerepo, side commit at 10:00:02 vs substantive at 10:00:01): `git log --format=%H HEAD` lists 'side content' before 'substantive change', and lwb_lanes.resolve_reviewable_head returned cd98e2f (the side commit) instead of 5249934 (the substantive one). MATCHES EXPECTED: False.

So the intermittent red is not noise and not mine: it is the walk-all-parents bug that PR #63 ('lwb_lanes: resolve_reviewable_head must walk first-parent history only') is open to fix, surfacing about a third of the time. This is PRE-EXISTING ON MAIN and is NOT caused by PR #69 -- #69 touches neither lwb_lanes.py nor that test. It matters beyond a flaky CI run: resolve_reviewable_head decides which sha a review record must name, so on any branch carrying a merge it can bind the gate to a side-branch commit. It does not affect THIS review: PR #69's branch is linear, and I computed the reviewable head both ways (all-parents and first-parent) for all 13 open PRs before choosing -- they agree on every one, and on #69 both give 8ae32b2.

A second, smaller near-miss: I initially read several gate exit codes through `| tail`, so those "exit=0" readings were tail's status rather than the script's. I re-measured every gate without the pipe before recording anything here; the corrected run is what this record rests on. That re-measurement is also what showed lwb_check_env_leak.py correctly failing CLOSED (exit 1) when unconfigured, which I had briefly mis-read as a pass.
